title: Shell command injection via unsanitized tag in deploy()
body: deploy(tag) builds a shell command with an f-string embedding the caller-supplied tag and runs it via subprocess.run(..., shell=True, check=True). Any caller of deploy() that passes an attacker-influenced tag (e.g. a Git tag/release name pulled from a webhook, PR title, or user input in a CI pipeline) allows arbitrary shell command injection on the deploy host. A tag value containing a shell metacharacter sequence such as a semicolon followed by a destructive command, or command substitution syntax, executes attacker commands with whatever privileges the deploy process holds (often cluster-admin kubectl credentials). Fix: never use shell=True with interpolated input; call subprocess.run(['kubectl', 'set', 'image', 'deploy/api', f'api={tag}'], check=True) as an argv list (matching the pattern already used in rollback()), and validate tag against a strict allowlist such as a semver/tag regex before use.
